severity: decision
description: Recovering probe's suppressed pairs by letter-splitting costs `n + C(n,2)` clashscore invocations — ~45 min per model on the 6-conformer 7KR0 (one run is 121 s), unaffordable per candidate model on 4 CPUs. **Decision: two-tier.** (i) Every candidate model gets the cheap tier: one probe run + the network-aware post-filter, plus `autoref/clash_sweep.py`, a gemmi geometric sweep (0.4 s on 7KR0, 9 s on the 6-conformer model) that enumerates the cross-network cross-letter contacts probe structurally cannot report. (ii) The full `n + C(n,2)` recovery runs on the **final** model per target and on any model whose sweep is non-empty; both numbers are reported side by side. **Measured**: deposited 7KR0 has **30 protein-protein clashes probe cannot see** (overlaps 0.63–0.75 Å, occupancy weights to 0.36; worst is Glu A64 OE2(B) vs His A86 HE2(A), 0.754 Å at weight 0.357). 3TC7 and 3QUE have none (single/no altloc network). 7KR0-6conf has 16, all water-water at weights ≤ 0.013.

severity: guard
description: `altloc_networks` rule (c) lets altloc-tagged waters chain networks transitively, collapsing the 6-conformer 7KR0 to few components — correct for a globally 6-conformer model, but over-merging is the dangerous direction (merged networks *drop* real clashes). Every sweep therefore reports the count twice — full graph vs **backbone-bonding only, no water bridging** — with a per-kind breakdown. Deposited 7KR0: 30 (all protein-protein) vs 64 (43 protein-protein + 21 protein-water); the gap is what water bridging suppresses. Caveat recorded in code: on a globally multiconformer model the waters genuinely carry the coupling, so the bonded-only count degenerates (6-conformer 7KR0: 16 vs 12 347, almost all water-water) and the merged count is the defensible one. An earlier "assume nothing is coupled" ceiling was tried and discarded as physically meaningless (1 039 pairs on 7KR0 against a defensible 30).

That gap is held at `deferred` because its N-side anchor Asp176 scores RSCC 0.6309, under the frozen 0.70 floor. severity: **bug found (not patched — another agent's file)**
description: `tools/real_space.py::refine_local` asks `phenix.pdbtools` for `output.filename=<cwd>/region.pdb` and then tests `cut.exists()`. Given an **mmCIF** input model, `phenix.pdbtools` 2.1-6048 ignores the requested extension and writes `region.cif`: the cut itself succeeds (3QUE, "Size before: 2850 size after: 24 … Job complete", exit 0) but the existence check fails and `RealSpaceError` is raised, so every mmCIF-based local refinement is reported as a tool failure. The canary never caught it because it feeds `7KR0.pdb`. Proposed patch, immediately after the cut: `cut_out = next((q for q in (cwd/"region.pdb", cwd/"region.cif") if q.exists()), None)`; raise only when `not rc.ok or cut_out is None`; then `cut = cut_out`. Worked around in `stages/discrete.py::model_for_local_refine`, which hands the local refinement a PDB copy — free here, since `refine_local` already splices into and returns a PDB, but it does cap the loop at models PDB can express, and it raises loudly rather than truncating if one cannot.

Reading: the operator's gain (0.1172 → 0.0662, D011) does not come from a handful of correctly placed local alternates — it comes from representing every residue as six copies, which is what `phenix.ensemble_refinement` does with more members (D425) but here in a form that refines and deposits as a multiconformer model. Neither qFit route (D440, D453) builds this. Consequence for the campaign: a **k-state whole-molecule model** (E022) is the representation to build — k complete conformers, one constrained occupancy group per copy, refined jointly — from an ensemble of the target (E023 for 7KR0; the 3QUE ensemble exists). Its own measurement of that model's R-free on our flags is running (`refine_zero`, `runs/7KR0.sixconf_rfree.log`) so the record is quoted from our pipeline, not the file header.

severity: **verified: the operator's 7KR0 six-conformer model scores R-free 0.0673 on the campaign's flags with the campaign's evaluator — the like-for-like record, by our numbers**

Our campaign model: 0.1137 full / 0.1157 report. The gap of **0.046** is on identical data and flags and is therefore the target's real, reachable record — the first such number in the campaign (3TC7's published figure is on other flags, D430; 3QUE's is an ensemble, D425). severity: **negative result (E022, 3QUE): freezing an ensemble into k complete copies makes R-free much worse — a k-state model needs its coordinates refined, not just its occupancies**
description: E022 on 3QUE, k=6 uniform (cycle 65) and k=4 population-weighted (cycle 66): k-medoids of the 25 ptls-0.8 ensemble members (all-atom RMSD, mean inter-cluster 1.0 Å), the medoids written as complete altloc copies A.. with one jointly-refined constrained occupancy group. Both built cleanly (17025 / ~11500 atoms, occupancy sums exact) and refined to **excellent geometry** (bond 0.002 Å, angle 0.57°) — copies average out — but R-free-select regressed hard: k6 attributable **+0.0444** (candidate 0.2995 vs null 0.2550), k4 **+0.0255**; `model_vs_data` agrees (+0.029 / +0.026). Ledger rows 65/66 `rejected` (regressed). Split-residue density 239/346 pass; the failure is R-free, not the gates. **Why (corrected 2026-09-05):** first read blamed frozen coordinates; that is wrong — the candidate arm's strategy was `individual_sites+individual_adp+occupancies+tls`, so the copies' xyz DID refine (verified in the command.txt). The real cause is **data-to-parameter ratio**: k=6 multiplies the atom count ~6× and 3QUE at 2.7 Å does not have the reflections to support it (k=4 regresses less, +0.0255 vs +0.0444 — monotone in k, the signature of over-parameterisation, not a bad start). The operator's 7KR0 six-copy model (D454/D455, 0.067) works because 0.77 Å has ~10× the data of 2.7 Å. **Consequences:** (1) a k-state model is only viable at high resolution — test it on 7KR0 (0.77 Å), not 3QUE; (2) test small k first (k=2, 3) and let the data choose, since even 7KR0 may not support 6 discrete copies (its base is already 89-residue multiconformer and whole-protein qFit failed there, D453). E022b = k-state on 7KR0 at k∈{2,3,6} from its ensemble (E023).

section: PROTOCOL §10 (compute and budget — GPU escalation recorded as a deviation)

severity: **bug fixed: k-state builder made duplicate atom labels on an already-multiconformer base (7KR0); short ensembles usable, k-state retried**
description: E022b on 8x (g424, 96 cores): three short ensembles (ptls 0.6/0.8/1.0, EQ_NTX=2/ACQ_NTX=4/tx=0.3, ~35 models each, ~1 h) built cleanly and score on our flags full R-free 0.151 / **0.147** / 0.171 — rough (under-equilibrated) but that is the k-state SOURCE, not the candidate. severity: **wall reached on the standard-tool routes at 0.77 Å; qFit completion test running, then pivot to learned generators**
description: Consolidated state of the conformer-generation push on 7KR0: (a) selective ensemble distillation from the short (rough, 0.147) ensemble regressed +0.0213 (rejected) — like k-state (+0.020, D463) and every ensemble→discrete transform; (b) the FULL ensemble has now failed to complete THREE times (7.5 h, 11 h, 20 h+), each hanging at 100 % CPU in the final non-solvent-B/assembly stage — phenix.ensemble_refinement does not finish on this 0.77 Å model in the time available; (c) composite_omit_map is intractable here (a full omit refinement per region at 0.77 Å; killed after producing only intermediates, no map); (d) per-residue qFit stalls at 0% sampling (D440 revisited) — a 15-min timed A9 test is running to settle whether qFit EVER completes/builds alternates here. Reading: the 3TC7 water-addition cycles are the campaign's overfit-risk zone, and the 7KR0 multicopy models widened the gap by 12–20σ while improving R-free-select — exactly the pattern the monitor exists to catch. Configurations tried before freezing (thresholds_v4 header): the v1 absolute rule; k·σ on base → candidate (fires on re-refinement alone); k·σ on candidate → null (adopted).

severity: **rule change by version: `thresholds_v8.yaml` = v7 + `paired.metropolis` (enabled, T = 1.0·σ_select, band (0, +k·σ]) — a `no_change` paired cycle whose attributable ΔR-free-select is worse but within +k·σ keeps its treatment arm with probability exp(−Δ/T) from a recorded deterministic draw; promotion additionally requires the credited best base not to be worse than the standing record on R-free-select; `scripts/run_dpdb.sh` defaults to v8**
description: Origin: Marcus Collins's review of the 2026-09-16 write-up ("rejecting negative results is a tricky business, statistically speaking … some amount of Monte Carlo/Metropolis") and Spencer's question whether a specific test decides when a credited model replaces the current one. Reading of the harness as it stood (v1–v7): `paired.decide_verdict` credits ≤ −k·σ, bisects > +k·σ, and in between D411 keeps the treatment arm iff attributable ≤ 0 — a hard boundary at zero inside a band whose width is the measured noise of exactly that comparison, so +0.5σ and −0.5σ are the same evidence and the rule prefers the changes that were lucky on the consulted half; greedy descent on a noisy objective stops at the first plateau. Change: `autoref/metropolis.py` (pure, tested) — p_keep = exp(−Δ/(temperature_sigma·σ_select)), u = sha256(target, cycle_index, seed) → [0,1), keep iff u < p; applied in `paired.run_paired_cycle` only when the frozen thresholds carry `paired.metropolis.enabled`, only for `no_change` with 0 < attributable ≤ k·σ, never when a gate (R-gap, divergence) has refused the candidate. Unchanged: the credit bar, the regression bar and its bisection, the R-gap gate (D495), the divergence gate (D497), the geometry/clash/RSCC gates, D484 (promotion on credit only). Bound: the SPEC_DPDB_RUNS §2 drift guard (cumulative un-credited drift > +k·σ → every kept change row `rejected`, base ← last credited base) is now armed after every Metropolis keep as well; the last-credited pointer is the run's start base until the first credit, so the walk can never end below the start model (a missing pointer falls back to the run's best base by R-free-select; `_track_best` now runs at cycle 0). Record: the decision (p, u, T, kept) is in `paired_cycle.json`, `cycle.json["metropolis"]` and DECISIONS.md. Promotion (Spencer's question, the test that exists): `_promote` moves `state/current/<T>.json` only when (a) the run credited something (D484), (b) NEW: the run's best base is not worse than the standing record on R-free-select (a tie from a different model is refused; re-writing the same model is not a replacement) — a credit is relative to the run's own null arm, not to the deliverable — else a `PROMOTE-<T>-c<N>` deviations row, and (c) the deliverable's R-gap does not widen beyond 2σ_gap (D495). Of the 13 credits on record, 7 moved a deliverable (3QUE c031, c041; 3TC7 c011, c057; 7KR0 c033, c035, c037); the 6 that did not: 3TC7 c058 (E029, beat its H-free null, worse than c057 on report/full), 3TC7 c064 and c068 (deliverable gap bound, D495/D498), 7KR0 c017/c019/c021 (sampleworks distillation credited against their own null arms at 0.226/0.124/0.126 full, above the 0.113 deliverable; never promoted because experiments do not promote). Retro-judgement (`state/exports/cycles.csv`, today's noise-floor rows σ_select 3QUE 0.00144 / 3TC7 0.000084 / 7KR0 0.000405, seed 1): of 84 paired cycles, 17 were `no_change` with 0 < attributable ≤ 2σ (3QUE 8, 3TC7 3, 7KR0 6); Metropolis at T = 1σ would have kept 9 of them (3QUE c033 +0.05σ, c036 +0.11σ, c038 +0.34σ; 3TC7 c031 +0.49σ, c053 +0.40σ; 7KR0 c003 +0.95σ, c032 +0.60σ, c040 +0.01σ, c041 +0.18σ) and dropped 8 (all four 3QUE cycles at +1.8σ, 3QUE c083, 3TC7 c025, 7KR0 c001, c042); no credit, no promotion and no deliverable would have changed, because those follow from the credit bar alone. Tests: `tests/test_metropolis.py` (6), `tests/test_run_discrete.py::test_metropolis_keep_is_uncredited_and_bounded_by_the_drift_guard`, `::test_promotion_refused_when_credited_base_is_not_below_the_standing_record`.
